entries.title: Bigme B6 Pro Color Review
entries.summary: The Bigme B6 Pro is a compact 6-inch e-reader powered by Android 14, offering full access to the Google Play Store, a sharp display, and expandable storage. The post Bigme B6 Pro Color Review first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Bigme B6 Pro Color is a premium, pocket-sized 6-inch color E-Ink e-reader and paper tablet. Released globally as a major upgrade over standard compact e-readers, it blends a retro, blocky design with advanced internal hardware and unprecedented refresh speed. It runs an older version of Android 14, but you can install apps via Google Play.

Hardware

The Bigme B6 Pro features a 6-inch Kaleido 3 color e-paper screen, presenting crisp monochrome text at 300 PPI and color content at 150 PPI. Boasts an industry-leading refresh rate of 75-85 FPS, drastically minimizing ghosting and enabling incredibly smooth web browsing, comic panning, and video playback.

The Bigme B6 Pro features a highly customizable 36-level adjustable dual front-light system. It uses white and amber LEDs on the side bezels to direct light across the screen, providing glare-free, paper-like illumination that emits zero blue light and remains flicker-free.

Under the hood is a MediaTek Dimensity 1080 processor, 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of internal storage. It also has a MicroSD card slot that supports up to 1 TB of additional storage. It supports dual-band Wi-Fi (2.4GHz / 5GHz) and Bluetooth 5.1. Built-in high-definition Hi-Fi stereo speaker and dual-microphone array with integrated GPT AI voice transcription. It is powered by a 2,100 mAh battery.

Supports an active capacitive pen that charges via USB for handwriting, sketch note-taking, and PDF document markup. Built-in local GPT artificial intelligence models capable of real-time multi-language voice transcription, text generation, document translation, and one-click meeting summaries. Bigme uses something proprietary with this pen; we tried 15 different pens, and nothing else worked on the screen.

Software

The Bigme B6 Pro runs on Android 14 and provides full access to the Google Play Store, letting users install third-party applications like Kindle, Chrome, and Moon Reader Pro. As noted in reviews from eWritable and TechRadar, the software interface includes custom speed and refresh rate profiles—such as a high-refresh Hyper mode—to optimize e-ink performance for different tasks like reading or web browsing.

Despite Android 14’s flexibility, reviewers note that the native skin and built-in reading tools feel unpolished and unfinished out of the box. Users on platforms like Reddit generally agree that the software experience improves significantly once you bypass the default reading app and configure third-party alternatives. The system also features a customizable capacitive touch strip at the bottom of the screen that can be mapped to shortcuts or navigation commands.

Overall, the software bridges the gap between a traditional e-reader and a mini Android tablet, though it requires some personal setup to shine. While the inclusion of advanced e-ink center controls and AI features adds functional depth, some users find the stock software ecosystem cluttered compared to simpler dedicated readers.

Reading

With a 6-inch 300 PPI E Ink display and 150 PPI for Colour content, this is a great e-reader. It includes a stock reading app that works well for sideloaded content. It supports all major formats, so you can quickly load your collection of e-books, PDFs, manga, or other digital content. The default reading app offers a range of functionality, including font size, Typesetting, Text Contrast, and Picture Contrast. The latter two create an interesting scenario, as the device treats the two elements differently and lets you set text and picture contrast independently. The device also lets you change settings and view the effects live in the background. It’s like sliding the Font Size option to its maximum position and seeing the change take effect on the page in the background.

PDF files look simply fabulous. Quality and speed are top-notch, with pages turning extremely fast. Note-taking is instantaneous, with almost zero latency. Also, since it runs Android, complete with Play Store support, you can install any PDF reader you prefer. That said, the stock software that comes with the PocketNote 2 Color does a great job, and you are unlikely to encounter any issues with it reading PDF files.

Wrap Up

The Bigme B6 Pro Color is a compact 6-inch e-reader powered by Android 14, with full access to the Google Play Store, a sharp display, and expandable storage. While it offers a versatile alternative to traditional dedicated e-readers by breaking free from single-store ecosystems, its heavy OS results in a less polished interface and shorter battery life.

The included stylus for the Bigme B6 Pro Color receives widespread criticism for its awkward size, poor pressure sensitivity, and lack of functional shortcuts. The pen has a small, slippery, and awkward shape that doesn’t dock inside the device body and cannot magnetically snap to the side. While it features a USB Type-C charging port and a tip-removal clip, carrying it relies on an awkward dangling magnetic case loop. The redesigned stylus lacks a physical eraser button or secondary shortcut key, forcing users to manually select on-screen tool options instead.

entries.title: Mudita is working on a series of E INK Apps
entries.summary: Mudita is working with developers on a series of E-Ink apps for their Kompakt phone. The post Mudita is working on a series of E INK Apps first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
MuditaOS K 2.0 brings custom launchers, Google Calendar sync, and curated E-Ink apps to the Mudita Kompakt minimalist phone. This new OS update will be launching sometime this fall and will be a free upgrade.

Key Features of MuditaOS K 2.0

Custom Launchers: Switch between the Kalm and Standard launchers. Choose between text or buttons for your home screen layout. You can also protect specific apps with a PIN.

Google Calendar Sync: Sync your schedule with a two-way Google Calendar connection. View plans and add new events directly on your phone.

InkApps & App Management: Browse InkApps, a curated collection of E-Ink-optimized apps created by Mudita and the community. Manage and organize your Android apps more easily.

Enhanced Customization: Set custom ringtones and adjust your Offline+ Mode settings to fit your daily focus needs.

Customize Offline+ Mode: Decide what going offline means to you. Control exactly what the mode switches off: choose separately whether Bluetooth and the camera remain available when Offline+ is on.

Personalize & refresh screen: Choose from new artistic wallpapers made specifically for Kompakt’s E Ink display. If you notice ghosting, use Force Refresh to clear the screen manually.

entries.title: XTEINK X4 Classic e-reader is now available for $79
entries.summary: The XTEINK X4 Classic is now available; however, it has several cons, and the XTEINK X4 Pro might be the better buy. The post XTEINK X4 Classic e-reader is now available for $79 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The XTEINK X4 Classic (also known as the X4 V2) is an ultra-portable, pocket-sized E Ink eReader designed for distraction-free, on-the-go reading. It is a streamlined second version of the original X4, removing complex smartphone features to focus on a lightweight, tactile reading experience.

The XTEINK X4 Classic features a compact 4.3-inch E Ink display housed in an ultra-thin body that weighs approximately 68 grams. Sticking to a distraction-free physical layout, it omits both a touchscreen and a front light, opting instead for front and side buttons for all navigation, as highlighted in a detailed review. The device also includes a magnetic backplate for easy integration with everyday carry.

Under the hood, an upgraded ESP32-S3 processor and a 920 mAh battery deliver longer battery life. For storage, it comes with 16 GB of internal capacity, expandable via a microSD card slot, and supports standard reading formats such as EPUB, TXT, MOBI, and PDF. Wireless connectivity features include built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. The XTEINK X4 Classic has pogo pins and uses a magnetic pogo-pin connection instead of a standard USB-C port.

One of the most interesting aspects of this device is how it handles page turns. Shake the device for easy one-handed reading during busy commutes, or use the tactile physical buttons for a cozy, deep-reading escape. However, if you don’t want to shake it to turn pages, you can disable that setting.

This e-reader is now available for $79 on the XTEINK website.

entries.title: XTEINK X4 Pro is now available on Amazon
entries.summary: The XTEINK X4 Pro is finally available on Amazon.com, making it much easier to purchase or return than buying directly from the XTEINK website. The post XTEINK X4 Pro is now available on Amazon first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The XTEINK X4 Pro pocket-sized e-reader is now listed on Amazon for the first time, giving people another option besides buying directly from the company. Amazon is the preferred way to buy XTEINK products, since they don’t accept returns or sell damaged products directly from their own e-commerce store.

The X4 Pro features a 4.3-inch E-Ink touchscreen with a resolution of 220 PPI. The lighting system is the most anticipated upgrade. It lets you read comfortably in the dark or in low-light environments without a separate clip-on reading lamp. Despite adding layers for the light and touch sensors, the Pro model measures an incredibly slim 5.98mm, making it slightly thinner than the original X4’s 6.4mm. It retains its physical page-turn buttons alongside the new touchscreen, giving you tactile control when flipping pages.

It has 16 GB of fixed internal memory for reading e-books, plus an SD card slot that supports up to 256GB. It has a paltry 8MB of RAM, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. It is powered by a 1100mAh battery, which should last a month of reading. Unlike the standard USB-C on the first-generation X4, the X4 Pro uses a magnetic, bespoke pogo-pin charging cable.

entries.title: Ugreen Gallery 3 Photo frame is coming out soon
entries.summary: Ugreen is releasing a 13.3-inch Gallery 3 digital photo frame that uses AI to upscale photos for an E-Ink screen. The post Ugreen Gallery 3 Photo frame is coming out soon first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Ugreen Gallery is a newly announced 13.3-inch color E Ink digital picture frame that debuted at IFA 2026. It is designed as part of Ugreen’s newly unveiled local AI smart home ecosystem, Ugreen HomeAgent.

The Ugreen Gallery is a 13.3-inch digital picture frame featuring an E Ink Spectra 6 full-color e-paper display with a native resolution of 1600 x 1200 pixels (4:3 aspect ratio). Because e-paper technology only consumes power when changing the image, the frame offers exceptional energy efficiency, enabling cordless operation and zero display glare under ambient light.

For local storage, it includes a microSD card slot supporting capacities up to 512GB, along with built-in Wi-Fi connectivity for seamless data transfers. A standout feature is its integration into the Ugreen HomeAgent local AI smart home ecosystem. Instead of relying on public cloud storage, the frame connects to a local hub that uses on-device AI to securely analyze your private photo libraries, automatically curating and casting daily highlights and memorable moments. Originally debuted at IFA 2026, the frame carries a promotional preorder price of $299 USD and an expected standard retail price of $439 USD.

entries.title: Onyx Boox Picco will cost $100 and release by end of 2026
entries.summary: The upcoming Onyx Boox Picco will not have Android, but it will have page-turn buttons and a physical front light. Slated to come out by the end of the year and cost $100.00. The post Onyx Boox Picco will cost $100 and release by end of 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Onyx Boox Picco debuted at IFA in Berlin. This is where most upcoming tech products make their official debut, often launching by the end of the year or early 2027. The Picco has some new details from journalists who spoke with the company at the conference. The device will run Linux instead of Android and will cost around $100 when it launches in the next few months.

The Onyx Boox Picco introduces a novel form factor to the digital reading world as an ultra-compact, pocket-sized micro e-reader. Sporting a tiny 3.97-inch grayscale E-Ink display, its smartphone-like footprint makes it uniquely portable, fitting easily into pockets where standard 6-inch e-readers cannot. Early hands-on previews praise its minimalist aesthetic, flat-bezel design, and built-in front light.

Storage will be limited to an SD card slot, and it appears to have no internal storage. This is where you will store e-books downloaded from the internet. Early reviewers have stated it will not have any DRM functionality, so you will have to rely on royalty-free or pirated content. You would turn the pages of an e-book using the up and down buttons on one side of the screen, and there is also a front-light button to turn it on or off.

The software at the event was limited. There was no audiobook player yet, so there would be no way to listen to audiobooks, podcasts, or music. There is no word on whether this will be included in the final release, and no information on whether the device will actually have Bluetooth functionality.

The inclusion of Linux is interesting; this is likely because the processor, battery, and RAM would be limited to meet the $100 price point. This would improve stability, but it would prevent users from installing their own apps. Onyx does not publish its OS and keeps everything internal, so this would limit the hacking community from installing things like Crossink or Crosspoint.

entries.title: Remarkable releases new Capture Tool
entries.summary: The reMarkable software update 3.28 is a major system release that introduces highly anticipated tools, color improvements, and reading enhancements to digital paper tablets The post Remarkable releases new Capture Tool first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Remarkable software version 3.28 introduces a new Capture Tool and improved color rendering. The Capture Tool allows you to circle and select any area of a document, then duplicate, resize, rotate, or move that content across different pages or notebooks. Improves color rendering for red tones on color-supported devices for ballpoint, fine-liner, and calligraphy brushes, eliminating the need for a screen-refresh flash.

The new software also moves the sharing menu to the main toolbar for quicker access, without opening the three-dot menu. The update also includes serious enhancements to the reading experience. Remarkable has updated the EPUB reading experience with a UI uplift, improved formatting, and expanded language support. The updated interface makes it easier to choose fonts and layouts, while the new font options help improve readability. Formatting tweaks ensure a better layout and presentation throughout your ebooks. Ebook thumbnails also look nicer.

You can take a look at the entire change log here.

entries.title: New TCL P80 phones have NXTPAPER AMOLED display
entries.summary: The TCL P80 Ultra and TCL P80 Pro are hybrid smartphones designed to blend premium display performance with dedicated, e-reader-style eye comfort. The post New TCL P80 phones have NXTPAPER AMOLED display first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The TCL P80 Pro and TCL P80 Ultra are newly released smartphones that seamlessly combine traditional smartphone functionality with the eye-comfort benefits of an e-reader. Both feature TCL’s revolutionary NXTPAPER AMOLED display, which offers a matte, anti-glare finish, circular polarization, and significantly reduced blue light emission.

Both phones have a physical side slider that instantly transforms the interface into “Max Ink Mode”. This black-and-white, low-distraction mode cuts off heavy notifications and allows the battery to last up to 7 days for reading books. Both include intelligent reading assistants that can convert standard text e-books into podcast-style audiobooks.

The TCL P80 Ultra and TCL P80 Pro share identical foundational hardware centered around a 6.83-inch 1.5K (2772 x 1280) eye-friendly NXTPAPER AMOLED display. This matte, low-glare screen supports a fluid 120Hz refresh rate, 3,200 nits of peak brightness, and a physical chassis toggle to activate a low-power, monochromatic “Max Ink Mode”. Under the hood, both devices pack a massive 5,800mAh battery that supports 45W fast charging, 8GB of RAM, up to 512GB of internal storage, and an IP68 and MIL-STD-810H durability rating. They launch with Android 16 and a comprehensive software commitment of four major OS upgrades alongside seven years of security patches

The main hardware difference between the two models is their processing power and camera arrays. The flagship TCL P80 Ultra runs on the more capable MediaTek Dimensity 7400 Elite processor. It stands out with a versatile triple rear-camera setup: a 50MP main sensor with OIS, an 8MP ultra-wide lens, and a dedicated 50MP periscope telephoto lens with 3x optical zoom. Conversely, the mid-tier TCL P80 Pro scales back performance and imaging to hit a more affordable price point. It uses the lower-tier MediaTek Dimensity 7300 processor and omits the telephoto lens, dropping to a simpler dual-camera setup that keeps the same 50MP main and 8MP ultra-wide shooters.

The official launch prices for the TCL P80 series vary slightly by region and storage capacity. The TCL P80 Pro will cost approximately $500 to $580, and the TCL P80 Ultra will be $640 to $650. Both models are slated to hit regional markets and global storefronts like Amazon throughout September 2026.

entries.title: E Ink Carta 1400 might be pushed back to 2027
entries.summary: Industry sources have told Good e-Reader that the E INK Carta 1400 will be delayed until 2027, meaning Kaleido 4 and Gallery 4 won't be released anytime soon. The post E Ink Carta 1400 might be pushed back to 2027 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E-Ink’s Carta 1400 was previously rumored to debut later this year, but supply-chain sources have told Good e-Reader that the tech won’t be ready for mass production until later in 2027. E-Ink’s largest partners, including Foxconn, which makes the Amazon Kindle; Netronix, which manufactures Kobo and NOOK e-readers; and Linfiny, which focuses on B2B, have received samples of the new screen technology to see how it will fit into future e-readers.

E-Ink still has no Carta 1300 white papers or product listings on its own website, and the tech has been part of mainstream Kindle and Kobo e-readers for years. No information explains what Carta 1400 will bring to the table. Rumors suggest it will push the standard optical contrast ratio past 20:1 for crisp text. Lower latency will make page turning, scrolling, and handwriting feel much closer to an iPad or paper note. Higher contrast ratios deliver crisp, “truer” blacks and ultra-bright whites to maximize outdoor and low-light readability. Refined waveform technology to drastically minimize text ghosting and the dramatic “black flash” associated with full e-ink screen refreshes.

E INK Carta 1300 was known as an incremental, generation-on-generation refinement of Carta 1200. While Carta 1200 was a massive, ground-up architectural overhaul that introduced significantly faster refresh speeds to the e-paper industry, Carta 1300 builds on that same foundation to deliver slightly better contrast metrics and lower latency.

The delay of Carta 1400 will cascade to Kaleido 4 and Gallery 4, which are in the prototyping stage. This color E-INK technology will not come out until Carta 1400 is used in e-readers such as the Amazon Kindle Paperwhite and other black-and-white e-paper e-readers of the future.

entries.title: Acer Announces New ePaper Monitor
entries.summary: The Acer EP130K ePaper monitor is a portable, touch-enabled 13.3-inch display introduced at IFA 2026. The post Acer Announces New ePaper Monitor first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Dasung, Bigme, and several other brands have been involved in the e-paper monitor business for a long time. Recent entrants such as Philips failed to gain traction because demand was low. Acer hopes to leverage its household name with the Acer EP130K ePaper monitor that offers a paper-like visual experience ideal for reading and deep work, plus touch support, up to 3200 x 2400 resolution, and both color and black-and-white modes. It uses a Kaleido 3 e-paper display from E INK.

Combining the natural viewing experience of paper-like visuals with glare-free use, the new Acer EP130K is designed for professionals who perform deep work for long periods, avid readers, and mobile users whose work takes them outdoors. The monitor supports touch directly on its ePaper screen, enabling stylus use and the intuitive feel of writing or drawing with a finger. It delivers up to 3200 x 2400 resolution with a 60 Hz refresh rate, and offers both color and black-and-white modes to switch between as needed. A single USB Type-C cable supplies power from the host device to the low-power-consumption panel, while its bistable functionality keeps the on-screen image in place even when all power sources are removed.

The Acer EP130K ePaper monitor starts at $749.99 USD in North America, €749 in EMEA, and $1,499 AUD. It will launch in these markets in early 2027.
